decisions.difference: A: (or Seizure Post-ictal state)  vs  B: Seizure
decisions.reason: The page's entry is "Confirm that patient indeed had a seizure/fit"; post-fit drowsiness and confusion are listed only as supporting features, so Post-ictal state alone is not the page's trigger.

decisions.difference: A: Post-ictal state in the priority and meningitis rules' seizure anchor  vs  B: Seizure only
decisions.reason: Follows the trigger decision: the red box sits under the Yes of "had a seizure/fit".

decisions.difference: A: no condition  vs  B: Frequent headache
decisions.reason: The page says "headache getting worse/more frequent"; A dropped "more frequent".

decisions.difference: A: (no (Epilepsy + Known present))  vs  B: (no Epilepsy)
decisions.reason: The page says "no known epilepsy"; Will's briefing writes known chronic conditions with Known present, and the HIV half of the same bullet already uses it. Two gate false positives are declared as known issues.

decisions.difference: A: Weakness of face muscles, Muscle weakness of limb, Numbness of face, Numbness of limbs + Sudden onset + Unilateral  vs  B: Muscle weakness, Numbness + Sudden onset + Asymmetry
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Muscle weakness" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Sudden onset" "qualifier value")) (qualifier (snomed_concept "Asymmetry" "qualifier value"))) ; same for Numbness
decisions.reason: The red box says "asymmetric weakness or numbness" with no site, so the generic concepts plus Asymmetry match its words; they also cover the No branch's "face, arm or leg" (A's concepts are descendants).

decisions.difference: A: Difficulty talking, Visual disturbance (no qualifier)  vs  B: both + Sudden onset
decisions.reason: In "New sudden asymmetric weakness or numbness, difficulty speaking or visual disturbance" (and "...face, arm or leg; difficulty speaking...") the comma/semicolon separates the items, so "sudden" grammatically attaches to weakness/numbness only; the page doesn't settle whether it distributes.

decisions.difference: A: (<= (onset Postpartum state) (time_ago 1 weeks)) alone  vs  B: (and Postpartum state (<= (onset Postpartum state) ...))
decisions.reason: "up to 1 week postpartum" needs both the postpartum state and the window; B states the presence explicitly, same meaning.

decisions.difference: A: Cerebrovascular accident only  vs  B: Cerebrovascular accident and a second rule for Transient ischemic attack
decisions.reason: The page says "Stroke or TIA likely"; both diagnoses are named and there's no joint concept.

notes: Both builds passed. Base is B (it covered "more frequent" headache and the TIA half of "Stroke or TIA likely"); rule descriptions are B's. From A: Epilepsy + Known present for "no known epilepsy" (which brings A's two declared gate false positives), and unqualified Difficulty talking / Visual disturbance. Everything else was identical in both builds: meningitis as Seizure AND any one of the four (questioned), the >= onset convention for "> 1 hour after fit", BP as systolic OR diastolic, and the common faint rule. Remaining questions from both builders are merged.
